mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks from its trough of -64.6 to -60.1, indicating a self-reinforcing recovery in foot traffic as households gradually resume discretionary errands. This momentum is expected to persist, pushing the next four-week mean above the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -64.6 at t-2w to -60.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next four-week RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the last four-week mean despite the prior three-week upward trend, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises week-on-week while WORKPLACES simultaneously falls, this signals an incoming tightening of movement restrictions (consistent with holiday-period containment measures), which will suppress retail and recreation visits over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises more than 0.5 points WoW while WORKPLACES falls more than 1 point WoW
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased from 16.0 to 16.4 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to decline over the next two weeks after RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls jointly, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together, commuting-linked routines resume jointly, generating compounding spillover into retail footfall that exceeds what either series would predict alone, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise concurrently for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -60.1 to -55.9 and WORKPLACES improved from -52.7 to -47.1 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks despite concurrent increases in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In the pre-Christmas shopping window, households increase retail visits for gift purchases regardless of baseline restriction levels, producing a short-term seasonal bump in RETAIL_REC over the coming week even as other indices remain depressed.
evidence_refs: fact:snapshot date 2020-12-15 falls within the pre-Christmas shopping period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following the snapshot despite the approaching Christmas period, the seasonal shopping hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Anticipated nationwide holiday-period restrictions (effective late December through early January) will force closures or capacity limits on retail venues, driving RESIDENTIAL higher and WORKPLACES/TRANSIT lower, which will compound to depress RETAIL_REC over the full four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains persistently elevated around +16 to +17 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or remains stable over the next four weeks despite the onset of holiday-period restrictions, the policy-driven suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in PARKS mobility signals increased outdoor leisure activity, which correlates with broader willingness to leave home and is expected to translate into higher nearby retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -47.9 at t-1w to -38.0 at t-0w, a rise of 9.9 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks following a PARKS jump exceeding 8 points, the outdoor-activity spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with a failure of TRANSIT to recover indicates sustained homebound behavior; together these reinforce reduced willingness to travel for non-essential retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the full four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 while TRANSIT remains below -50 for all four snapshot weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 16.0 and 17.1 while TRANSIT stayed between -60.1 and -54.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL and TRANSIT both remaining in their depressed/elevated bands, the homebound-behavior hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As the Christmas holiday nears, households shift spending toward grocery and pharmacy stockpiling rather than general retail and recreation outings, causing GROCERY_PHARM to rise relatively faster than RETAIL_REC and signaling a near-term dip in RETAIL_REC growth within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -34.1 at t-2w to -27.3 at t-0w, outpacing the RETAIL_REC recovery rate
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following the snapshot despite GROCERY_PHARM improving faster than RETAIL_REC, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.
